segments.say: Let's slow down a little more now. There's nothing to sort, nothing to measure, and nothing to work out. Tonight, we spent a long while looking at personality from the outside, the way a scientist might. Now let's look at it the way a tired traveller looks at the hills at the end of a long walk. Softly, from a distance, with no need to name anything.

First, let yourself settle. Feel the weight of your head on the pillow. Feel your shoulders resting, and your back, and your legs. Let the bed hold all of it. You don't have to hold yourself up anymore tonight. Something underneath you is doing that work now, quietly and without complaint, and it will keep doing it all night long.

Now take one slow breath in, through your nose, if that's comfortable. Not too deep. Just a little fuller than before. And let it go, slowly, as if you were letting out a long, quiet sigh at the end of the day. There. That's all. You don't need to count, or to get it right. Your body already knows how to breathe.

Let's do that again, together, very gently. Breathe in, slowly. Pause, just for a moment, at the top. Breathe out, longer and softer. And rest, in the stillness before the next one. Breathe in. Pause. Breathe out. Rest. If you lose the rhythm, that's perfectly fine. Just let your breath find its own way, like water finding the lowest path.

With every breath out, let something small go. The tightness in your jaw. The little frown between your eyebrows. The thoughts still humming in the back of your mind. You don't need to push them away. Just let each breath out carry a tiny piece of them off into the dark, the way a slow tide carries a leaf back out to sea.

Now picture yourself standing somewhere high and quiet, at dusk. Maybe a grassy rise, or the edge of a gentle valley. The air is cool and soft. The sky is fading from gold to a deep, calm blue. In front of you, a wide landscape stretches out, rolling and quiet, all the way to the horizon. There's nobody else here. Just you, and the evening.

And imagine that this landscape is you. Not a map, not a chart, not a list of scores. Just a soft countryside, with hills and hollows and long, quiet fields. Each gentle hill is one of your traits. Some rise a little higher. Some are low and rounded. None of them are wrong. Together, they make a view that belongs only to you.

Perhaps there's one hill, over to the left, where the paths wander off in every direction. That's your curious side, the part of you that likes new ideas, new places, new songs. It might be tall, or it might be small and comfortable. Either way, the evening light rests on it gently, the same way it rests on everything else in the valley.

Over there, perhaps, is a neat, steady hill, with tidy hedges and a little path that winds carefully to the top. That's the part of you that plans, and finishes things, and remembers. Some evenings it feels tall and strong. Some evenings it feels a bit overgrown. Tonight, it doesn't need tending. It can simply sit there in the dusk.

Let your eyes travel slowly across the whole view. The hills, the hollows, the long soft fields between them. Notice how none of the hills compete with each other. None of them are trying to be the tallest. They're just resting side by side, under the same wide sky, while the light fades slowly from their tops, one by one.

There may be a hill where voices carry easily, where the paths lead down towards a little village with lit windows. That's your outgoing side, the part of you that reaches towards other people. Next to it, perhaps, there's a quiet wooded hill, where it's peaceful and still. Both are lovely. Both are part of the same land, and both belong here.

And somewhere, there's a warm, green hill, with soft grass and shady trees, where travellers could rest. That's the kind side of you, the part that listens, and shares, and forgives. It doesn't need to be the tallest hill in the view. It only needs to be there, catching the last warm light of the evening, the way it has all your life.

Sometimes, clouds roll over parts of the landscape. A little worry here. A small storm of feeling there. That's just weather. It moves across the hills, and then it moves on. The hills stay where they are underneath. And tonight, the sky is clear and calm, and the last of the clouds are drifting slowly away, towards somewhere else entirely.

Real hills change, too, though far too slowly to watch. Rain softens them. Grass grows over old paths. New trails appear where people walk often. Your landscape is the same. Over the years, the hills shift a little, gently and quietly, without any fuss. You don't need to see it happening. It's enough to know, here, tonight, that it does.

No hill needs to be the tallest. No valley needs to be filled in. The landscape is whole just as it is, with its high places and its low places and its quiet fields. You don't need to flatten anything, or build anything up, tonight. You only need to look at it kindly, the way you'd look at a place you love.

show.text: No hill needs to be the tallest.

segments.say: Let your breath slow down a little more, as if the whole landscape were breathing with you. A long, slow breath in, like a soft breeze rising up the slope. And a long, slow breath out, like that same breeze sinking back into the valley. In, and out. The grass bending, and rising, and bending again. All of it peaceful. All of it yours.

Now watch the very last of the light leave the hilltops. First the highest ones, then the lower ones, until the whole view is a soft, deep blue. The edges of things grow gentle. The hills blur together into one long, rolling shape. You can't tell where one trait ends and another begins. And that's exactly how it should be.

Above the hills, the first stars begin to appear. One, and then another, and then a few more, small and quiet and very far away. They don't hurry. They don't announce themselves. They simply arrive, when the sky is ready for them. Let your thoughts be like that tonight. Arriving softly, and fading softly, with nothing at all to do.

And when you're ready, let the landscape fade gently, and come back to the room around you. The pillow. The blanket. The quiet dark. You can keep the hills with you, if you like, somewhere at the edge of your mind, a soft blue view to drift towards. They'll be there whenever you close your eyes and want to visit.

In a little while, we'll go softer still. We'll move slowly through the body, letting each part rest and soften, one at a time. There's nothing to prepare for it, and no way to do it wrong. If you fall asleep before then, that's perfect. That's what this time is for. Just keep breathing slowly, and let the night carry you.
